title: Margins, Revenue Quality & EBITDA in Practice
description: Practice analyzing profitability metrics, revenue recognition signals, and earnings quality using realistic business scenarios.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS company reports: Revenue up 30% YoY, but deferred revenue declined 15% YoY and accounts receivable doubled. What's the key signal?

options.text: Strong growth justifies the receivable increase
Revenue quality is suspect - future revenue pipeline is shrinking
The company is shifting from subscriptions to one-time sales
Cash collection timing is slightly delayed but normal

chartData.title: SaaS Company Key Metrics YoY Change (%)

interactions.prompt: EBITDA equals operating income plus ____ plus amortization, making it a proxy for operating cash generation before reinvestment.

options.text: Interest expense
Depreciation
Tax expense
Capital expenditures

interactions.prompt: You're evaluating two retailers. Company A has 42% gross margin but 5% operating margin. Company B has 28% gross margin but 12% operating margin. Which is the better-run business and why?

options.text: A - higher gross margin means stronger pricing power and brand
B - converts more gross profit into operating profit, showing cost discipline
A - gross margin is the most reliable profitability indicator
Neither - you need net income to compare operational quality

interactions.prompt: Nike reports Q3: Revenue $12.4B (up 5%), gross margin expanded 150bps to 45.0%, but SG&A grew 12% to $4.1B. Operating margin fell 80bps. What matters most?

options.text: Gross margin expansion shows strong product pricing momentum
SG&A growth outpacing revenue is eroding operating leverage
Revenue growth of 5% is the primary concern
Operating margin decline is temporary and seasonally normal

chartData.title: Nike Q3 Key Metrics - Year-over-Year Change

interactions.prompt: Rank these earnings quality red flags from MOST concerning (first) to LEAST concerning when analyzing a manufacturer's income statement.

options.text: Revenue growing while cash from operations declines for three years
One-time restructuring charge of 2% of revenue
Changing revenue recognition policy to recognize sales earlier
Gross margin declined 50bps due to raw material inflation

interactions.prompt: A PE firm is acquiring a software company. The target reports $80M EBITDA but capitalizes $18M of software development costs annually (amortized over 5 years). A comparable company expenses all development. How should you adjust?

options.text: Use reported EBITDA - capitalization follows GAAP rules correctly
Reduce EBITDA by $18M to ~$62M for apples-to-apples comparison
Add back amortization, raising EBITDA further above $80M
Ignore EBITDA entirely and use only free cash flow

interactions.prompt: You're assessing a hospital chain's profitability sustainability. Rank these income statement analyses from MOST to LEAST important for predicting future margins.

options.text: Trend in payer mix between Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurance
Year-over-year change in depreciation expense
Operating margin trend over the past five years by segment
Labor cost as a percentage of revenue versus peers

interactions.prompt: The software target just disclosed that 40% of its $200M revenue comes from a single government contract expiring in 14 months with no renewal guarantee. How does this change your profitability analysis?

options.text: No change - analyze current profitability and assume contract renews
Stress-test margins assuming $80M revenue loss and high fixed cost base
Exclude the contract revenue entirely from valuation
Reduce EBITDA margin by 40% proportionally across all line items

interactions.priorContext: Previously you valued a software company at $80M adjusted EBITDA on $200M revenue. Now a major customer concentration risk has been revealed.
